The plan covers services only if they are described in this section, are not listed as an exclusion here or in the General plan exclusions, do not exceed limits in the schedule of benefits, are medically necessary (see the Medical necessity and precertification requirements section), and are not prohibited by law. For outpatient prescription drugs you must have a prescription from the prescribing provider and show your ID card at a network pharmacy. Some services require precertification; covered services are listed alphabetically, but absence from the list or a specific “not covered” entry does not automatically mean a service is not covered—check your provider or contact the plan and consult the schedule of benefits for limits and cost-sharing. Examples and exceptions: physician care is generally covered but cosmetic surgery is excluded; home health care may be limited to a set number of visits per year; experimental, investigational, or unproven services are excluded unless part of an approved clinical trial for cancer or a terminal illness; preventive services are generally paid at a higher plan benefit—see the Preventive care section and schedule of benefits for details. Covered services include abortion services provided by your physician, including abortion drugs dispensed by a provider. Coverage explicitly includes drugs dispensed via telemedicine providers. Coverage is subject to and limited by applicable state and local laws (only where permitted). Acupuncture is covered only when provided by a physician as a form of anesthesia in connection with a covered surgical procedure. Acupuncture for any other purpose (non‑anesthetic) is not covered. Acupressure is also explicitly not covered.

Emergency ambulance transport is covered when your condition is unstable and requires medical supervision and rapid transport; coverage is limited to licensed ambulances and only to the first facility to provide emergency services or to another facility if the first cannot provide the needed emergency services. Non-emergency ambulance transport is covered only when an ambulance is the only safe way to transport you, limited to transport to the nearest facility able to treat your condition and to ground ambulance transport from a facility to your home. The policy also lists as not covered: ambulance services for non-emergency transportation and ambulance services for routine transportation to receive outpatient or inpatient services. (The document therefore both limits non-emergency coverage to “only when the ambulance is the only safe way” and separately states non-emergency ambulance services are not covered.) Covered services include applied behavior analysis (ABA) for members with a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder. ABA is defined here as a process of applying interventions that systematically change behavior and that are responsible for observable improvements in behavior. Autism spectrum disorder is defined in the most recent edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM). Covered services include services and supplies provided by a physician or behavioral health provider for the diagnosis and treatment of autism spectrum disorder. Coverage also includes physical, occupational, and speech therapy when associated with the diagnosis.

Coverage includes treatment for mental health and substance‑related disorders when provided by a hospital, psychiatric hospital, residential treatment facility, physician, or behavioral health provider and applies to both inpatient and outpatient settings. Inpatient coverage pays room and board at the semi‑private rate (a private room is covered when medically appropriate) plus other services and supplies during the stay. Outpatient coverage includes office visits (including telemedicine) to psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers, licensed professional counselors, individual/group/family therapies, partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient programs, ECT, TMS, psychological and neuropsychological testing, observation, and peer counseling support. Skilled behavioral health services in the home are covered only when all criteria are met (you are homebound; physician orders them; they replace a hospital/residential stay or cannot be provided outside the home; and they are appropriate for active treatment). For substance‑related disorders the outpatient list also explicitly includes ambulatory/outpatient detoxification. Peer support by a peer support specialist is covered but must be supervised by a behavioral health provider.

Routine patient costs from a provider related to participation in an approved clinical trial (as defined in the Public Health Service Act, Section 2709) are covered. Not covered are services/supplies solely for data collection or record‑keeping, items provided free by the trial sponsor, and the experimental intervention itself (except Category B investigational devices and certain promising experimental or investigational interventions for terminal illnesses per plan policy). Coverage of experimental or investigational drugs, devices, treatments, or procedures in a clinical trial is limited to members with cancer or a terminal illness and requires that standard therapies are ineffective or inappropriate and the plan determines the member may benefit. An “approved clinical trial” must meet all requirements: FDA approval or IND/group treatment IND status when required, institutional review board (IRB) approval, sponsorship by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) or similar federal organization conforming to that organization’s standards, be conducted at an NCI‑designated cancer center or at more than one institution, and the member must be treated according to the study procedures. Durable medical equipment (DME) and necessary accessories are covered when items are built for prolonged use, primarily treat illness or injury, are suited for home use, are not normally used by people without an illness/injury, and are not intended to alter air quality/temperature or for exercise/training. The plan covers only the types of DME that Medicare covers (but excludes some Medicare-covered items) and pays for renting or buying DME from a supplier; purchases are covered only if needed for long-term use. Also covered: one item for the same or similar purpose, repairs for normal wear and tear, new items needed because a member’s physical condition changed, and replacement of items damaged by normal wear when replacement is cheaper than repair or renting a similar item. Not covered: communication aids, elevators, repairs from misuse/abuse, massage tables, personal voice/message recorders, over‑bed tables, portable whirlpool pumps, sauna/sauna baths, telephone alert systems, vision aids, and whirlpools.

For an emergency medical condition, go to the nearest emergency room or call 911/local emergency response for medical or ambulance help. Covered emergency services are limited to outpatient services in a hospital emergency room to evaluate and stabilize an emergency medical condition and may be provided by network or out‑of‑network providers. Coverage for emergency services continues until you are evaluated and stabilized and your attending physician determines you are medically able to travel or be transported by nonmedical/non‑emergency transportation to another provider. If the physician admits you to the hospital (emergency admission) or requires follow‑up care, those are not emergency services and different benefits, medical necessity and precertification rules apply; ER visits that are not for an emergency medical condition may not be covered (see schedule of benefits). Covered services include certain services and supplies for gender affirming treatment; coverage is limited to services that meet the plan’s criteria. Some cosmetic procedures related to gender affirming care are covered—members should call Member Services (number on the back of the ID card) for specifics. For full details on eligibility and medical necessity requirements, refer to Aetna’s clinical policy bulletins at https://www.aetna.com/health-care-professionals/clinical-policy-bulletins.html or call the toll‑free number on the ID card. Habilitation therapy services are services needed to keep, learn, or improve skills and functioning for daily living (e.g., a child not walking or talking at expected age) and must follow a specific treatment plan ordered by your physician. Services must be provided by a licensed or certified physical, occupational, or speech therapist; a hospital, skilled nursing facility, or hospice facility; a home health care agency; or a physician. Outpatient physical and occupational therapy are covered only if expected to develop any impaired function; outpatient speech therapy is covered only if expected to develop speech function that resulted from delayed development. Not covered: services provided in an educational or training setting or to teach sign language, and vocational rehabilitation or employment counseling.

Hearing aids are defined as any wearable, non‑disposable instrument or device to aid or make up for impaired hearing, including parts, attachments, or accessories. Covered services include prescribed hearing aids and an audiometric hearing visit/evaluation for a hearing aid prescription when performed by a physician certified as an otolaryngologist or otologist, or by an audiologist who is legally qualified in audiology, holds an ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence when no licensing exists, or who performs the exam at the written direction of a legally qualified otolaryngologist/otologist. Electronic hearing aids installed in accordance with a prescription written during a covered hearing exam and other related services necessary to access, select, adjust, or fit a hearing aid are covered. Not covered are replacement hearing aids lost, stolen, or broken, batteries or cords, and hearing aids that do not meet the specifications prescribed for correction of hearing loss. Hearing exams are covered when performed by a hearing specialist for evaluation or treatment of illness, injury, or hearing loss. Exams performed during a hospital or other facility stay are not covered. Exception: newborn hearing exams provided as part of the overall hospital stay are covered. Home health care provided by a home health agency is covered in the home only when all criteria are met: you are homebound; a physician orders the services; they substitute for a hospital or skilled nursing facility (SNF) stay or you cannot receive the same services outside the home; they are part of a home health care plan; and they are skilled nursing, home health aide, medical social services, or short-term speech/physical/occupational therapy. Home health aide services must be supervised by a registered nurse; medical social services must be provided by or supervised by a physician or social worker; skilled nursing must be provided by a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse within their licensed scope. After a hospital or SNF stay the intermittent requirement may be waived to allow continuous skilled nursing (see schedule of benefits); short-term therapies in the home are subject to the same conditions and limits as therapy provided outside the home. Not covered: custodial care, services provided outside the home (e.g., in conjunction with school, vacation, work, or recreational activities), and transportation.

Covered hospice services, when provided as part of a hospice care program, include inpatient and outpatient hospice care such as room and board; services and supplies; hospice agency- or hospital-provided services; psychological and dietary counseling; pain management and symptom control; bereavement counseling; and respite care. Hospice services provided by non‑employee providers are covered, including physician consultation/case management, physical and occupational therapy, and services from a home health care agency (physical/occupational therapy, medical supplies, outpatient prescription drugs, psychological and dietary counseling). Services expressly not covered include funeral arrangements; pastoral counseling; financial or legal counseling (including estate planning and drafting a will); and homemaker/caretaker or other services not solely related to care (for example sitter/companion services, transportation, and house maintenance). Inpatient and outpatient hospital care are covered. Covered items explicitly include semi-private room and board (the plan will cover the extra expense of a private room when appropriate because of your medical condition), services and supplies from a hospital outpatient department including the facility charge, services of physicians employed by the hospital, and administration of blood and blood products. The policy excludes all services and supplies provided in rest homes, any place considered a person’s main residence or providing mainly custodial or rest care, health resorts, spas, and schools or camps.

Basic infertility coverage is limited to provider visits to diagnose/evaluate the underlying medical cause of infertility and surgical treatment of that underlying cause (e.g., endometriosis surgery, varicocele surgery). Not covered are all services associated with ovulation induction cycles using injectable medications (including related imaging, laboratory, and professional services), intrauterine/intracervical insemination (IUI/ICI), and all services tied to Advanced Reproductive Technology (ART) cycles (e.g., IVF, ZIFT, GIFT, cryopreserved embryo transfers, gestational carrier cycles, and related procedures such as ICSI or ovum microsurgery). Also excluded are cryopreservation, storage, and thawing of eggs/embryos/sperm/reproductive tissue; surrogacy-related charges; purchase of donor embryos/eggs/sperm or obtaining sperm from a person not covered under the plan; home ovulation prediction kits and home pregnancy tests; and injectable infertility medications (e.g., menotropins, hCG, GnRH agonists). Infertility treatment is also excluded when a successful pregnancy could have been obtained through less costly treatment, when infertility results from voluntary sterilization (with or without reversal), or when infertility is due to natural physiologic processes such as age-related ovarian insufficiency (e.g., unmedicated FSH ≥ 19 on cycle day 2 or 3 or other abnormal testing per Aetna's infertility clinical policy). For infertility benefits beyond this basic coverage, contact Progyny (www.progyny.com or 1-844-930-3295). Aetna Institutes of Quality (IOQ) is a network of publicly recognized, high-quality, high-value facilities/clinics that offer access for specific procedures and have met extensive quality and cost-effectiveness criteria. The IOQ program applies only to adult members (age 18 and over) and includes facilities participating under standard Aetna contracts. Facilities are designated via a targeted Request for Information (RFI) process; designation is valid for two years provided the facility maintains compliance with IOQ program requirements.

Institutes of Quality Bariatric provides bariatric (weight-loss) surgery for people with morbid or extreme obesity, intended for patients who have not achieved long-term weight loss through other means. IOQ offers lap bands (a device wrapped around the upper stomach to restrict food intake), gastric bypass (creation of a small stomach pouch connected to the middle small intestine, bypassing the remainder of the stomach and upper small intestine), and sleeve gastrectomy (removal of the majority of the stomach to form a narrow tube that reduces intake and absorption). These procedures are presented as surgical options for significant, treatment-resistant obesity. Coverage is limited to the diagnosis and surgical treatment of jaw joint disorders provided by a provider, including conditions of the joint itself (for example temporomandibular joint dysfunction/ TMJ) and disorders involving the joint’s relationship with related muscles and nerves (for example myofascial pain dysfunction/ MPD). Non-surgical dental services and therapeutic services related to jaw joint disorder are explicitly not covered. Covered maternity services include pregnancy (prenatal) care, post-delivery care and obstetrical services. After birth the plan covers at least 48 hours of inpatient hospital care for a vaginal delivery and at least 96 hours for a cesarean delivery, unless the attending physician and the mother agree to an earlier discharge; if discharged earlier the plan pays for one home visit by a health care provider. The plan also covers services and supplies needed for circumcision. Services and supplies related to births that occur at home or in any facility not licensed to perform deliveries are not covered. Obesity surgery is available for people who are morbidly obese when a physician determines they qualify. Covered services include an initial medical history and physical exam, diagnostic tests given or ordered during the first exam, outpatient prescription drugs as specified under the outpatient prescription-drugs section, an obesity surgical procedure, multi-stage procedures when planned and approved by the plan, and approved lap-band adjustments in office or outpatient settings. Not covered are weight-management treatment and drugs intended to decrease or increase body weight or treat obesity except as described elsewhere in the booklet. Preventive care services for obesity screening and weight-management interventions are excluded regardless of related conditions; this exclusion explicitly covers drugs/stimulants/preparations, dietary and food supplements, appetite suppressants, hypnosis or other therapies, exercise programs/equipment, health/fitness-club membership, recreational therapy, and other activity-enhancement services.

Oral and maxillofacial treatment (mouth, jaws and teeth) is covered when provided by a physician, dentist, or hospital. Covered procedures include cutting out (excision of) cysts, tumors, or other diseased tissues. Cutting into gums and other tissues of the mouth is covered only when it is not associated with removal, replacement, or repair of teeth. Covered services: services and supplies used in connection with outpatient surgery performed in a surgery center or a hospital outpatient department. If the same surgery is performed in a physician's office, the plan pays only for physician/PCP services and does not pay a separate facility fee. Not covered: a hospital stay (see Hospital care) and services of another physician for administration of a local anesthetic. Covered physician services are those provided by your physician to treat an illness or injury and may be delivered at the physician’s office, in your home, in a hospital, at other inpatient or outpatient facilities, or via telemedicine. For behavioral health, any in-person covered service with a behavioral health provider remains covered when delivered by telemedicine. Telemedicine services may have a different cost share than other physician services (see your schedule of benefits). Additional physician-provided items explicitly listed include allergy testing and injections, radiological supplies/services/tests, and immunizations that are not classified as preventive care.

Outpatient prescription drug coverage is determined by the plan's drug guide; drugs on the formulary exclusions list are not covered unless you or your provider obtains an approved medical exception. Pharmacists may refuse fills based on professional judgment and the plan applies routine safety checks; utilization review can restrict coverage (e.g., limit to one prescriber/pharmacy, quantities, partial fills, or denials). Coverage requires use of network pharmacies: retail fills are limited to 30-day supplies, mail-order maintenance drugs up to 90 days, and specialty drugs up to 30 days — all specialty fills (including the first) must be at a network specialty pharmacy unless urgent. Generic substitution may be used and synchronization is available with prorated daily cost share; a copayment assistance program can eliminate specialty drug cost share after you meet your deductible, though assistance amounts generally do not count toward your deductible or out-of-pocket limit unless the drug is an essential health benefit. In emergencies or when out-of-area, you may pay full price at an out-of-network pharmacy and submit a refund form (reimbursement is limited to emergency-related items and will be reduced by your network cost share). The plan covers many preventive items (FDA-approved contraceptives, certain OTC preventive drugs, immunizations, diabetic supplies, tobacco-cessation and weight-loss drugs under specified conditions), but lists many exclusions and limits (e.g., compounded prescriptions with non‑FDA bulk chemicals, cosmetic drugs, most dietary supplements/medical foods, certain injectables and administration charges, off‑label use except as supported by peer‑reviewed literature, dental-prescribed drugs, replacement of lost/stolen prescriptions); exceptions may be granted per the plan's policies.

This plan follows preventive-care guidelines from ACIP (CDC), USPSTF, HRSA and AAP/Bright Futures; updates become effective on Jan 1 one year after issuance. Covered preventive services include counseling (e.g., alcohol/drug misuse, tobacco cessation, obesity/nutrition, STI, genetic risk for breast/ovarian cancer), routine physicals and well-woman visits (including Pap smears, BRCA testing, postpartum diabetes screening, urinary incontinence screening), prenatal routine exams and listed pregnancy screenings, and routine cancer screenings (colonoscopies with polyp removal and pathology, DRE, DCBE, FOBT, lung screening, mammograms, PSA, sigmoidoscopy). Breast-feeding support and counseling are covered when delivered by a certified breast‑feeding support provider; coverage for breast‑pump equipment is limited to one item (plus necessary accessories/supplies) and additional similar items are your cost. Family-planning coverage includes contraceptive counseling and devices when prescribed/provided/removed by a health professional and female voluntary sterilization (excluded: follow-up care for sterilization complications, FDA-reviewed-but-not-approved contraceptives, and male contraceptives/sterilization). Preventive immunizations are covered; immunizations required for employment or travel are not considered preventive. Diagnostic testing or services not listed as preventive may be covered separately and could require higher cost-sharing; contact your physician or the plan for frequencies/limits or see healthcare.gov.

A prosthetic device replaces all or part of an external body part lost or impaired by illness, injury, or congenital defect. Covered benefits include physician-ordered initial provision and subsequent replacement, plus instruction and services (e.g., attachment/insertion), and repair/replacement when you outgrow the device, your physical condition changes, or due to ordinary wear and tear or damage. A prosthetic provided as part of another covered service is excluded from this benefit. Specific exclusions: orthopedic or therapeutic shoes (except when an orthopedic shoe is an integral part of a covered leg brace), trusses/corsets/other support items, and repair or replacement due to loss, misuse, abuse, or theft. Covered services include all stages of reconstructive breast surgery and related supplies provided by your provider in an inpatient or outpatient setting only when reconstructing the breast after a necessary mastectomy. Coverage explicitly includes implant and areolar reconstruction, surgery on a healthy/contralateral breast to achieve symmetry, treatment of physical complications arising from any stage of the mastectomy (including lymphedema), and prostheses. Covered services include all stages of reconstructive surgery and related supplies in inpatient or outpatient settings only in specified circumstances: when the surgery implants or attaches a covered prosthetic device; when surgery corrects a gross anatomical defect present at birth that causes severe facial disfigurement or major functional impairment and the purpose is to improve function; or when surgery is needed because treatment of an illness caused severe facial disfigurement or major functional impairment and the surgery will improve function. Accident-related procedures/surgery to sound natural teeth injured in an accident are covered if performed as soon as medically possible and the teeth were stable, functional, and free from decay or disease at the time of injury, and the procedure returns the teeth to pre-accident function. Those dental accident services are limited to the first placement of a permanent crown or cap for a broken tooth, the first placement of dentures or bridgework to replace lost teeth, and orthodontic therapy to pre-position teeth. Cardiac rehabilitation is covered when provided at a hospital, skilled nursing facility, or physician's office only if it is part of a treatment plan determined by the patient’s risk level and ordered by a physician. Pulmonary rehabilitation is covered during an inpatient hospital stay when ordered by a physician as part of the treatment plan. Outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation may be covered if performed at a hospital, skilled nursing facility, or physician's office, is used to treat reversible pulmonary disease states, and is part of a physician-ordered treatment plan.

Short-term rehabilitation services must follow a specific treatment plan ordered by your physician and be performed by a licensed/certified physical, occupational, or speech therapist; a hospital, skilled nursing facility, or hospice facility; a home health care agency; or a physician. Covered services include spinal manipulation (provider must establish/approve a treatment plan specifying treatment, frequency and duration), and physical, occupational, and speech therapy only when each is expected to significantly improve or restore functions lost due to an acute illness, injury, or surgical procedure (occupational therapy may alternatively help relearn skills for activities of daily living; speech therapy also covers correcting congenital gross anatomical speech delays). Cognitive rehabilitation is covered only when deficits are caused by neurologic impairment from trauma, stroke, or encephalopathy and the therapy is coordinated with the insurer as part of a treatment plan intended to restore prior cognitive function. Outpatient short-term PT/OT/SLP are subject to the same conditions and limitations in the schedule of benefits; services in educational/training settings (including teaching sign language), vocational rehabilitation, and employment counseling are not covered. Covered services include inpatient skilled nursing facility care. Coverage specifically includes room and board (limited to the semi‑private room rate) and services and supplies furnished during a skilled nursing facility stay. Specialty prescription drugs are covered when they are purchased by your provider or when they are injected or infused by your provider in an outpatient setting, including a freestanding outpatient facility, the outpatient department of a hospital, a physician’s office, or by a home care provider in your home. A complaint is for dissatisfaction with a provider or an operational issue and should be submitted to Member Services by phone or in writing with a description and any supporting records; the plan will review and provide a written response within 30 calendar days of receipt (and will request additional information if needed). An appeal is a request to re‑review an adverse benefit determination and may be filed verbally or in writing. Complaints and appeals are distinct: complaints address service/operational problems, while appeals challenge benefit determinations. Providers may submit claims or request prior approval before, during, or after you receive a benefit. While many claims are paid at the full rate (less your cost-share), some claims may be paid only in part or denied; any denial, even partial, is an “adverse benefit determination” (or “adverse decision”) and triggers a written explanation of benefits. You may request an internal appeal (a review of the adverse determination) and, if still dissatisfied, pursue further appeal. In most cases you must complete both levels of internal appeal before taking other actions (for example requesting an external review), although there are limited situations where you may skip the two internal levels. You may appeal an adverse benefit determination; appeals are assigned to a reviewer who was not involved in the original decision and must be filed within 180 calendar days of receiving the notice. File an appeal in writing to Member Services at the address on the notice or by calling the phone number on your ID card, and include your name, employer name, a copy of the adverse benefit determination, your reasons, and any other information to consider. Another person (an authorized representative), including a provider, may submit an appeal for you — you must notify the plan and are asked to complete an authorized representative form (available from the plan); authorized representatives may be used at any level of appeal. You may appeal twice; a second appeal must be submitted within 60 calendar days of receiving the first appeal decision. For urgent or pre-service claims a provider may appeal on your behalf without an authorized representative form; the plan will provide any new or additional information it used or developed to review your claim at no cost before issuing the final adverse benefit determination, and you may respond before the final decision.
